headline: Meta has bought Assured Robot Intelligence, a small startup that builds AI brains for robots, to speed up its humanoid robot programme.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a confirmed acquisition, but a small team with no price disclosed.
importance_line: What changed is that Meta now owns one of the few teams teaching robots to read and adapt to human behaviour, which matters to the workers whose jobs humanoids are meant to do, then to the robotics labs losing talent, then to Meta and Amazon in their race, and the doubt is that no price, product or timeline was given.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Stocktwits, that Meta has completed the purchase of Assured Robot Intelligence, a startup building AI models that let robots understand and adapt to people around them, with a Meta spokesperson confirming the deal as part of its humanoid robot effort. The founders, Lerrel Pinto and Xiaolong Wang, join Meta Superintelligence Labs to work alongside Meta Robotics Studio; Pinto's previous company, Fauna Robotics, was bought by Amazon in March 2026 for the same purpose, and no price was disclosed.
notes: Source credited to Bloomberg, the first reporter; Stocktwits page is where the text was read because the Bloomberg link could not be found or opened. No machine shown doing anything: an acquisition, so machine_action false.
